turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, obs before you go in. Pulse is 114, blood pressure 126 over 74, temperature 36.6, oxygen sat 99 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, sweet. Heart always ticks a bit fast when I'm just sitting around. Not a drama.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. Doctor'll grab you in a tick. Have a seat.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen's gone to lunch. Uh. What's been going on?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Didn't really need an appointment. Dropped a bit of weight, that's the whole story.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That's not the whole...
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm eating more than usual too, which is backwards, I guess. Still fine.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? The inbox just jumped over my note. Eating more, and losing weight?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Eating heaps. Weight's down a bit. I'm not worried.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did the weight start coming off?
[SEG0011] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Ugh, the parking meter's probably expired, I should've... sorry. You tell him.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, last winter. Or the one before. Maybe since the grand final, or after. I honestly can't date it.
[SEG0013] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He's been sweating through his shirts, and his hands shake when he holds a cup.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Kitchen's hot, that's all the sweating is. Hands are a tiny bit shaky. Whatever.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): The fast heart, is that part of this or just you being nervy in the chair?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): It races now and then. Thumps in my chest. Settles if I sit down. It's nothing.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah. No pain.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Short of breath on a shift?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah. Not short of breath.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bowels playing up, any runs?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Gut's normal.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else going on with the waterworks?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. All normal.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fevers at all?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No temperature. Just the sweats, and they're nothing.
[SEG0027] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He was going to skip the shakes entirely, they've been...
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): They're nothing, I already said.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history. Thyroid, sugar, blood pressure, anyone?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, my older sister's got thyroid disease, she's on carbimazoll or whatever they call it. My father had diabetes in his fifties, mum did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar. That's the lot.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold on, it didn't save. Older sister, and your dad, once more?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Older sister, thyroid disease. Dad had diabetes in his fifties. Other sister, pressure, no sugar. Mum didn't.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work, the hours, what you eat, exercise, grog? I'm still on the wrong tab, so go slow.
[SEG0034] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He'll play it all down if you let him...

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a barista at a little cafe in Brunswick. Six days, roughly fifty hours, early starts. Diet's whatever's left in the cabinet, mostly toasties and the odd takeaway. Exercise, I used to jog and I don't anymore, maybe a walk if the shift finishes early, and alcohol's a couple of beers Friday and Saturday, not through the week.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Couple of beers, was that every night? Sorry, clicked the wrong thing.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends. Friday and Saturday. Like I said.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets? File's still spinning.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing regular. I'm not a tablet person.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies to anything?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Nup. No allergies.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hands out. Yep, fine shake in both hands, palms are a bit damp. Pulse is rapid and regular, I can't hear a murmur. Neck doesn't feel particularly enlarged.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): See. Nothing to write home about.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): My working thought is an overactive thyroid, but I can't call it till the bloods are back. I'll send you for thyroid function tests and a full blood count today, and an ECG while you're here. If you get chest pain or you faint, don't sit on it, straight to emergency. Come back next week and we'll go through it.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Palpitations were described as 'thumps in my chest' that occur now and then and settle if he sits down.
Negative finding asked and answered: no urinary symptoms / 'waterworks' all normal.
Medication history: no regular tablets / not taking any regular medication.
Safety-net advice included going straight to emergency if he faints.
